newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-weak -dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-weak -dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady with a weak tone amid outlooks for lighter demand and some packers' plans for a small weekend slaughter, livestock dealers said.
However, price pressure from the lighter demand could be offset by projections for fewer hog marketings on Thursday and Friday, they said.

Light demand was seen fostered by continued weak packer operating margins as earnings from a recent increase in pork prices failed to keep up with the cost of buying the hogs and producing the pork, dealers and packer buyers said.
Marketings were seen declining in part because of forecasts for continued heat and humidity in the Midwest into the weekend.

Movement also could be lighter because many farmers sold a larger than expected number of hogs on Tuesday, some ahead of schedule, to take advantage of prices above $60.00 per cwt in much of the Midwest, sources said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen at $61.00, possibly $61.50.
Top Illinois hogs were seen at $60.50/plant and top prices for Indiana/Ohio hogs were expected at $61.00, dealers said.
